sections.html:
Vienna is the seat of this rural central Georgia county. Lilly, Byromville, Pinehurst, Unadilla and Vienna are cities, and Dooling, Drayton and Findlay are towns. Unadilla is the largest.

About 11,156 people lived here in 2025, a drop of 0.5% from April 2020, spread across 4,906 housing units. Only 22 building permits were issued in 2025. Roughly 64.7% of homes are owner-occupied, and the typical owned home is valued at $107,400, with median gross rent at $758.

Farm, small-town and acreage properties make up nearly every sale, so the Vienna county offices end up handling most of the paperwork.

A seller will deal with three county offices. The first two share 105 W. Cotton Street in Vienna.

Dooly County offices
OfficeLocationPhoneHours
Tax Commissioner105 W. Cotton Street, Room 1; mailing address P.O. Box 371229-268-4212Mon to Thu, 7:30 a.m. to 6 p.m.; closed Fri
Assessors Office105 W. Cotton Street, Room 2229-268-4719Weekdays, 8 to noon and 1 to 5
Commissioners' Office113 N. Third Street, Room 1229-268-4228Call for hours

Online payment and tag renewal (through Georgia DRIVES) are linked from the commissioner's page. The office is closed Fridays, so schedule payoff requests and counter payments for Monday through Thursday.

The county's 2025 proposal was 17.45 mills. That is 0.445 mills above the no-increase rate of 17.005 mills and would bring in 2.62% more property tax revenue. Hearings took place at the commissioners' office, 113 N. Third Street.

The proposal was only a starting point, so ask the tax commissioner which rate your current bill uses.

Assessed value is 40 percent of fair market value, and mills are applied to that smaller figure. The county levy is just one line on the bill; school and city rates may be added for your parcel.

First call the Assessors Office, 229-268-4719. Each year the board mails a notice of assessment, and an owner who rejects the stated fair market value gets 45 days, counted from the mailing date, to file. The postmark has to fall inside that window.

  • You can argue taxability, value, uniformity or a refused exemption
  • The PT-311A form has you pick equalization board, hearing officer or arbitration
  • Emailing the form works only when the board has adopted a written policy for electronic service
  • Nothing is sent to the state revenue department

Filing instructions come with the notice, so save the envelope or write down the postmark date. If tax was collected by error or illegally, ask for a refund in writing within three years of paying.

Returns of value go to the county tax office between January 1 and April 1. Paid last year and filed nothing? Your value is simply carried over. For homestead, apply once the house is your primary residence and before April 1 of the first benefit year. A missed application forfeits that year.

Only the state exemptions apply, though the commissioner can tell you if anything extra exists. A tax information pamphlet with homestead details is linked from the commissioner's page; request a current copy rather than trusting older numbers.

A freeport exemption for commercial and industrial inventory is also possible if voters approve it, and you request it from the board of assessors during the return period. It matters to owners of a shop or warehouse, not a typical house.

A mobile home has its own paperwork. Georgia wants a location permit from the tax commissioner within 30 days of placement, with a renewal each year in the first quarter. A mobile home sitting in the county on January 1 is returned for taxation by April 1, together with the permit.

  • A mobile home on land you are selling needs its permit and return current
  • Vehicle registration renews with the commissioner in the 30 days ending on the owner's birthday
  • A newly bought vehicle needs registration within 30 days
  • Only the tax commissioner can collect motor vehicle tax

Have the commissioner confirm any mobile home's status ahead of the buyer's lender.

sections.h2: What taxes come due when a Dooly County house sells?
sections.html:
The ad valorem tax for the whole year lands on the person who owned the property on January 1, even if the sale happens in spring or summer. Splitting it with the buyer is a matter for the contract, and the settlement statement should show how.

Recording the deed brings Georgia's real estate transfer tax, which the seller owes and the closing agent works out from the state schedule. The buyer's long-term mortgage adds an intangible recording tax, and the security instrument is recorded locally within 90 days. County and state tax liens both go on the clerk's general execution docket.

Bills are normally due December 20 unless the county picks a different date, with interest held off for 60 days after the postmark. Get a payoff figure from the commissioner and pass it to your closing agent.

sections.h2: A short plan for selling a Dooly County property
sections.html:
Start in Vienna. Visit the commissioner Monday through Thursday for a written balance, then stop at the assessors' room for your parcel's value, any covenant and the status of every exemption. If a mobile home or an old permit is tied to the land, settle that account at the same time.

Hand the written balance to your closing agent so the payoff comes out of the proceeds. A cash buyer can usually close quickly in a county this small, but the title search for liens on the execution docket still happens.

Watch the calendar. The January 1 owner is billed, so a summer closing leaves the year's tax with you unless the contract shifts it. Have your agent or attorney put a proration clause in the contract, then check it against the settlement statement.

An estate sale needs one extra call. Ask the assessors which papers they want in order to change the owner and homestead record, and do it before the sign goes up. A record still showing the former owner can hold up the payoff letter.

Bills: 229-268-4212. Values: 229-268-4719. Keep both numbers handy.

If you are unsure whether a question is about money or value, ask the person at the first desk you reach and let them point you across the hall. Both offices work out of the same building in Vienna, so one trip can cover both.

faqs.q: When is the Dooly County tax office open?
faqs.a: Monday through Thursday from 7:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., and closed Friday. Find it at 105 W. Cotton Street, Room 1, Vienna, or call 229-268-4212.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to dispute a Dooly County value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days after the notice went in the mail. File in writing with the county board of tax assessors rather than the state, and call 229-268-4719 with questions.

faqs.q: Does Dooly County have a homestead exemption?
faqs.a: The state exemption is available, and no local add-on applies, so ask the commissioner about anything more. Apply by April 1 of the first year you want it, since a missed application waives that year.

faqs.q: What was Dooly County's proposed 2025 millage rate?
faqs.a: The county proposed 17.45 mills, an increase of 0.445 mills over a no-increase rate of 17.005 mills. Check your current bill with the tax commissioner for the rate in force.

faqs.q: Who owes the tax if my Dooly County house sells midyear?
faqs.a: The person who owned it January 1 is liable for the full year under Georgia law. A contract can pass part to the buyer, so check the proration on the closing statement.
